quotes.text: Here in Ohio, we're being turned into a dumping ground for our nation's addiction to artificial intelligence. As these data centers come pouring in, not paying their fair share of taxes, not supporting local employment after the things get built.
And where automation technologies give us more time with our family, not fewer job opportunities.
It's just a lose, lose, lose, lose situation when these people of central Ohio are being asked to become a dumping ground for our nation's addiction to AI.

At the end of the day, what we need is a bill of rights as a nation for these data centers. That means specifying how far they have to be from our communities. That means making sure that they're not jacking up our electricity prices or putting us in a downward spiral of carbon emissions and climate crisis with the amount of power that they consume.

I am not against all data centers, but I am against dumb data centers. I support technological development and balanced growth, but central Ohio should not be turned into a dumping ground for our nation’s addiction to AI.

That is why I support a national moratorium on new construction and a data center bill of rights that includes distance prohibitions against encroachment on farms and residential neighborhoods, promotes local control over such siting decisions and ensures that the construction of data centers doesn’t adversely affect ratepayers or threaten our national power grid.
